title: How the Isaac Heeney salary compares to the National Minimum Wage: casual loading and super paid on top
description: Understand how the Isaac Heeney salary and any hourly rate convert to annual pay using 38 hours, casual loading, and super paid on top. Fair Work Commission rates included.
salarySummary: From 1 July 2026 the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour for a 38‑hour week, or $1004.90 per week, with casual loading of 25% ($33.05 per hour) and super paid on top.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 becomes $33.05 per hour for casual employees. When using [the timesheet](/), tick the casual loading checkbox to add 25% automatically – never type a rate that already includes loading.

faqs.q: Is superannuation paid on top of my hourly rate or included?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The Super Guarantee is 12% of your gross pay (up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year). So if your hourly rate is $30, your employer adds $3.60 per hour to your super account, not to your take‑home pay.

faqs.q: What hours per week does the calculator assume?
faqs.a: The calculator assumes a standard 38‑hour week, which is the full‑time ordinary hours used by the Fair Work Commission. You can adjust the hours if needed, but the annual conversion formula is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For a 38‑hour week, that’s hourly × 1976.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding your hourly rate and annual salary

Whether you earn the National Minimum Wage or a figure closer to the **Isaac Heeney salary** (the Sydney Swans star reportedly earns well over $1 million a year), every annual salary can be broken down to an hourly rate. The conversion is simple: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks.

For full‑time employees the standard week is 38 ordinary hours, as set by the Fair Work Commission. So the formula becomes:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × 38 × 52**

That’s 1,976 hours a year. If you’re paid a salary, dividing it by 1,976 gives your equivalent hourly rate. If you’re paid by the hour, multiplying gives your annual gross.

### The fortnightly view

Many Australians are paid fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. For a minimum‑wage employee on $26.44 per hour, that’s $1,009.80 per week (38 hours) or $2,019.60 per fortnight before tax and super.

## National Minimum Wage and award rates

From 1 July 2026 the National Minimum Wage is **$26.44 per hour** or **$1,004.90 per week** for 38 ordinary hours, according to the Fair Work Commission. This is the base rate for adult employees not covered by an award or agreement.

Most employees, however, are covered by a modern award. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes [pay guides](/blog) for each award, and from 1 July 2026 award minimum wages increased by 4.75%. Award rates are often higher than the National Minimum Wage, especially for skilled roles.

Even a high‑profile salary like the **Isaac Heeney salary** – reportedly in the range of $1.2 million per year – can be expressed as an hourly rate. Dividing $1,200,000 by 1,976 hours gives about $607 per hour. That’s more than 20 times the minimum wage, but the same conversion logic applies.

## Casual loading and super paid on top

Two important additions to your hourly rate are casual loading and superannuation.

### Casual loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not having paid annual leave or sick leave. For the National Minimum Wage, that’s **$33.05 per hour** ($26.44 × 1.25).

When using [the timesheet](/), tick the “casual loading” checkbox – the tool adds 25% automatically. Never type a rate that already includes casual loading, because you would double‑count it.

### Superannuation paid on top

Superannuation is not deducted from your hourly rate; it’s paid **on top** by your employer. From 1 July 2026 the Super Guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a minimum‑wage employee earning $26.44 per hour, the employer adds $3.17 per hour to super. For someone on the **Isaac Heeney salary** level, the employer would contribute the maximum $32,499.60 per year (12% of $270,830).

This means your total employment cost is higher than your gross pay. The [reference tables](/data) on this site show the super caps and rates.

## Example: from minimum to maximum

Let’s compare two scenarios:

| Item | National Minimum Wage | Isaac Heeney salary (approx.) |
|------|----------------------|-------------------------------|
| Hourly rate | $26.44 | $607.00 |
| Weekly (38 hours) | $1,004.90 | $23,066.00 |
| Fortnightly | $2,009.80 | $46,132.00 |
| Annual gross | $52,254.80 | $1,200,000.00 |
| Casual loading (25%) | $33.05/hr | $758.75/hr |
| Super (12% on top) | $6,270.58/yr | $32,499.60/yr (capped) |

Note: The **Isaac Heeney salary** figure is illustrative. Actual AFL player salaries vary and may include additional allowances not covered here.

## Tax and take‑home pay

Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident rates: nil up to $18,200, then 15% to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy is generally 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed).

For a minimum‑wage earner ($52,254.80), tax would be roughly $7,942 plus Medicare $1,045, leaving about $43,267 take‑home. For the **Isaac Heeney salary** level, the top marginal rate applies, and take‑home would be significantly lower as a percentage.

Use the [take‑home pay](/topics/take-home) page for a detailed breakdown.

## Using the timesheet

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate, choose casual loading if applicable, and see your weekly, fortnightly, monthly, and annual figures. It also estimates tax and super. Remember: super is shown as an employer contribution on top, not deducted from your pay.

Always check your award or agreement for the correct classification rate. The Fair Work Ombudsman’s Pay and Conditions Tool can confirm your minimum entitlements.

## Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
